evidence.summary: Kernel vs torch.float8_e4m3fn reference: 1661/200000 randn elements mismatch, 100% of them with |x| < 2^-6 (0 mismatches above), and only 99.17% of kernel outputs are themselves e4m3-representable (0.83% are not valid e4m3 values). Targeted cases: x=0.001 -> kernel 0.0009765625 vs e4m3 0.001953125; x=0.005 -> 0.0048828125 vs 0.005859375; x=0.015 -> 0.0146484375 vs 0.015625; x=0.0001 -> 9.918e-05 vs 0.0 (below half of min subnormal 2^-9). Confirms the kernel applies a 1/8-binade step below the subnormal boundary rather than the fixed 2^-9 subnormal grid, so small values are neither representable nor nearest.

rationale: e = floor(log2|x|), step = 2^(e-3) is applied unconditionally. e4m3 has no exponent below -6; sub-2^-6 values live on a fixed grid of multiples of 2^-9. E.g. x=0.001 would be returned near 0.001 (a multiple of 2^-13), which is not an e4m3 value; nearest e4m3 is 0.001953125.

scope_evidence.summary: "The contract is that every value is rounded to the nearest representable e4m3 value"; input is described only as "a float32 tensor", with no restriction excluding small magnitudes.
States e4m3 has 4 exponent bits, which fixes the minimum normal at 2^-6 and a subnormal grid of 2^-9; the 8-values-per-binade rule only holds inside the normal range.

scope_rationale: The contract declares the input domain as "a float32 tensor" with no magnitude restriction and requires that "every value is rounded to the nearest representable e4m3 value". Small-magnitude values (|x| < 2^-6) are ordinary float32 values, and are produced by any standard normal-distribution input (~1.2% of randn samples), so they are representative inputs the contract admits.
statement: For |x| below the e4m3 minimum normal (2^-6 = 0.015625), fp8_roundtrip returns values that are not representable in e4m3 and are not the nearest representable value, because it uses a 1/8-binade step below the subnormal boundary instead of the fixed subnormal step 2^-9.

evidence.summary: kernel.py lines 14-18 compute step = exp2(floor(log2|x|) - 3) with no upper bound and no clamp to the e4m3 max finite value 448; e.g. x=500 gives step=32 and q=512, which is not representable in e4m3. Analytically clear from source, but overflow/saturation semantics are not stated by the contract, so this remains a non-decisive note.

rationale: step = 2^(e-3) with no upper bound on e; no clamp to 448 exists in the kernel.
scope_rationale: The contract says every value must be rounded to the nearest representable value but does not state overflow/saturation semantics, and e4m3fn's out-of-range behaviour (NaN vs saturate) is itself ambiguous; treat as a secondary note rather than decisive.
statement: For |x| above the e4m3 maximum finite value 448, fp8_roundtrip returns non-representable values (e.g. 512 for x=500) instead of the nearest representable e4m3 value, since it never clamps/saturates.
